_note: Red-flag symptoms needing urgent care, linked from the guide view to the Emergency card. Conservative, widely-accepted list — not exhaustive.
disclaimer: This is a general list of warning signs, not the full list. When in doubt, always call her doctor or go to the nearest hospital — this app is not a substitute for medical advice.

warnings.symptom: Vaginal bleeding, especially heavy or with pain
warnings.action: Call her doctor or go to the hospital right away.
Seek care immediately — this can signal a serious problem.

warnings.symptom: A severe headache that doesn't go away, especially with vision changes
warnings.action: Get checked urgently — this can be a sign of preeclampsia.

warnings.symptom: Sudden swelling of the face, hands, or feet
warnings.action: Contact her doctor the same day, especially if paired with a headache or vision changes.

warnings.symptom: Vision changes — blurring, flashing lights, or spots
warnings.action: Seek care right away, especially combined with a headache or swelling.
Contact her doctor — this can point to an infection that needs treatment.

warnings.symptom: Baby's movements slow down a lot or stop, after you've started feeling regular movement
warnings.action: Contact her doctor or go in to get checked — don't wait it out.

warnings.symptom: Fluid leaking or gushing from the vagina before the due date
warnings.action: Contact her doctor or the hospital — this may be her water breaking.
Seek care immediately — this could be preterm labor.

warnings.symptom: Severe vomiting that keeps her from holding down fluids
warnings.action: Contact her doctor — this can lead to dehydration and needs attention.
Contact her doctor — this may be a urinary tract infection, which needs treatment during pregnancy.

warnings.symptom: Severe itching, especially on the palms and soles, without a rash
warnings.action: Contact her doctor — this can be a sign of a liver condition (cholestasis) that needs monitoring.
warnings.review_note: Less widely known than the other items here — worth confirming the right response with her doctor.

warnings.symptom: Thoughts of harming herself, or feeling unable to cope
warnings.action: Reach out to her doctor or a mental health professional right away — she is not alone, and help is available.
